root_cause: The production post-capture path joined render frame i to server tick i using index equality alone. It never checked that the screenshot for frame i was actually taken during tick i. The client screenshot pipeline can fall arbitrarily far behind the 20 Hz server tick stream, so a frame labelled tick i may depict a world many ticks later, while every downstream visibility, coordinate, and target decision reads that frame as if it showed tick i.
evidence_source: NON_SCIENTIFIC_INTEGRATION_REHEARSAL plus structural timestamp fields only
visible_consequence_in_rehearsal_ltr: Frames 0-9 are blank sky captured before world load. Frames 10-18 are one frozen partially-loaded render in which the occluding wall chunk is absent, so the magenta target is spuriously detected while standing inside the occluder footprint. Frames 19+ show the loaded world. Every visibility label derived from this capture is therefore invalid.
repair_scope: Add a fail-closed post-capture join-validity check. A captured frame must have been taken at or after its own tick was emitted and strictly before the next tick was emitted; otherwise the frame depicts a different world than the row it is joined to.
threshold_rationale: The bound is the next recorded server tick timestamp from the capture itself, not a tuned tolerance. No scientific quantity is decided by this check.

focused_test.command: qualified PATH/JAVA_HOME/PYTHONPATH python -m pytest -q tests/test_regime_a_production.py tests/test_regime_a_a4_runner.py tests/test_regime_a_magenta_adapter.py tests/test_regime_a_capture_alignment.py tests/test_regime_a_client_focus.py

detection_only_caveat: This repair makes a temporally invalid capture impossible to process silently. It does not by itself make the client screenshot pipeline keep pace with the server tick stream. Remediating the capture-side backlog remains an open blocker before any recapture.
